title: Main Deck Seat Track Sealing Standard for the Galley and Lavatory Zones
abstract: Proposal to extend the wet-zone track sealing practice to the main deck galleys and lavatories on the latest build standard, where the drainage arrangement differs and the earlier upper deck answers do not transfer.

sections.reason: The latest build standard changed the main deck galley drainage from a gravity run to a collected drain, and on the small number of aircraft delivered with that arrangement the collection tray discharges close to the seat track splice. Four aircraft have shown staining at that splice within their first three years, which is early. The upper deck answers do not transfer, because the main deck track sits on a different beam pitch and the collected drain did not exist when they were designed. Nothing has yet been found beyond staining and no structural finding has been reported.
sections.description: The scope is limited to the seat track bays under the main deck galleys and lavatories on the affected build standard. The inboard shear tie kit D5350113458608 at the beam interface is replaced by an item with a sealed web, and the lower cleat D5350130671217 at the cargo floor panel edge is renewed. A forward stringer kit DEL150648-53 is added to close the gap through which the tray discharge reaches the splice. Tubular spacers AGS113247-1C set the tray standoff, and the lower clip VA24289-25 retains the revised drain path. The change is confined to the fore and aft galley bays and the mid galley bay, zones 962, 972 and 983, and does not touch the seat track itself outside those bays. Detail is on drawing D53501314028.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 6 kg per aircraft. No electrical load change. The revised shear tie is not interchangeable with the original because the web is sealed and the drain path is different. No inspection relief is claimed, because no repeat inspection exists for this area on this build standard. Illustrated parts content for the main deck galley bay floor structure requires update, and the galley removal task changes at the drain disconnection step.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only, on the aircraft delivered with the collected drain arrangement. Provisional estimate is three days with the galleys out. No production cut-in is proposed, since no further aircraft will be built.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must confirm that the collected drain arrangement is the actual driver rather than the galley loading practice, and whether the change is worth doing at all on a population this small given that no structural finding has been reported.
